artifacts.synopsis: An appeal challenged a presbytery's conviction of a minister for divisive behavior and its indefinite suspension from office and the sacraments. The SJC affirmed: the charge was lawful because publicly publishing disagreement with the session after it acted violated his ordination vows to subjection and peace/unity, even though “divisive” is not a constitutional term; the censure was not unjust absent repentance; procedural errors did not require reversal or remand. A dissent argued the charge failed BCO 29-1’s Scripture-proof requirement.

artifacts.title: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church v. New River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church complained against New River Presbytery's action sustaining a complaint that a Sunday school teacher holding theistic evolution and other doctrinal exceptions should not teach. The SJC partially sustained the complaint, declining to refer the matter back to the church with instructions but advising that the teacher should not teach while he holds exceptions that could require him to teach contrary to the fundamentals of the system of doctrine.

artifacts.title: Session's right to access congregation's financial and attendance records

matches.evidence: CCB advised that the session and diaconate have a right to access financial and attendance records as needed, limited only by prudence and protection of reputation.

artifacts.title: Elder responsibilities and human sexuality language in BCO 8-3

matches.evidence: The CCB found no constitutional conflict in amending BCO 8-3 to incorporate AIC Report language on human sexuality for elder responsibilities.
